correctness.rationale: Exact fixed-point elimination gives R q(y)=1 on the physical x(y)>0 interval. G(s)=s[r+log(1-bs)] has strictly negative second and third derivatives; Q=s_double_prime/s_prime_squared has explicitly strictly negative derivative, and P=-G_double_prime/G_prime strictly increases while G_prime>0. Thus the curvature of T=G(s(y)) changes at most once, so W=yT_prime-T crosses zero at most once; its endpoint sign gives precisely one peak if c>1/2+b/r, otherwise strict decrease. The peak has strictly negative q_second, proving nondegeneracy. Direct symbolic differentiation, high-precision numerical example, and boundary checks support the proof; computation is not used as proof of the global count.

value.rationale: The 2026 motivating model expressly leaves the two-intersection ceiling unresolved. A unique unimodal stationary recruitment function yields a sharp fold count for every r>0,b in (0,1),c≥0 and β>0, excludes more complex equilibrium branch multiplicities, and identifies the previously omitted exact reproduction-number equality case. A complete natural classification of positive ecological fixed points is structurally motivated and nontrivial, independently of numerical diagrams or downstream stability theorems.
